overall: Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by convening in executive session without a roll call vote on September 20; the notice was found sufficient, and the amended minutes must be corrected.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the September 20 notice gave an insufficiently specific executive session topic (litigation strategy over an OML complaint).
allegations.key_passage: included sufficient information from which the public could conclude that the topic was appropriate for executive session; and therefore sufficiently advised the public of the anticipated discussion.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee did not take a roll call vote before convening in executive session on September 20; members raised hands instead.
allegations.key_passage: After reviewing a video recording of the September 20 meeting, we agree and find that the vote by the Committee to convene in executive session was not conducted by roll call.

allegations.summary: Committee amended the September 20 minutes to show a roll call vote to enter executive session that the AG found did not occur as recorded.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, we find that the Committee should not have amended the minutes of the September 20 meeting to reflect that the vote was recorded by roll call.

remedy: Revise the September 20 open session meeting minutes to accurately reflect the vote to convene in executive session, and certify to the AG within 30 days that it has done so.
Immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements; similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee to revise the September 20 open session meeting minutes to accurately reflect the vote to convene in executive session and certify to this office within thirty (30) days of the date of this letter that it has done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
